props.name: The results confirm Garner's suggestion that the irreversible adsorption of carb
props.note: the suggestion is cited from Garner; the confirmation is this source's
props.statement: The results confirm Garner's suggestion that the irreversible adsorption of carbon monoxide takes place on an acceptor site.

props.name: CO acts as an electron donor in the adsorption: raising the Fermi level with Ga2
props.statement: CO acts as an electron donor in the adsorption: raising the Fermi level with Ga2O3 decreased the heat of adsorption, and lowering it with Li2O so facilitated electron donation that reduction became too rapid to measure the adsorption.

props.name: Owing to the reduction effect the higher pressure sections of the CO isotherms a
props.statement: Owing to the reduction effect the higher pressure sections of the CO isotherms are of doubtful value, and the isosteric heats may be considerably in error at higher coverages.

props.name: The CO2 isotherms on all three adsorbents are typically chemisorption isotherms;
props.statement: The CO2 isotherms on all three adsorbents are typically chemisorption isotherms; chemisorption is confirmed by isosteric heats of 16-28 Kcal per mole.

props.name: The maximum CO2 adsorption measured (about 5 x 10-6 moles/m2) corresponds to a s
props.statement: The maximum CO2 adsorption measured (about 5 x 10-6 moles/m2) corresponds to a surface coverage of about one half, assuming an effective cross section of about 16 A2 for CO2 and SO2.

props.name: CO2 acts as an electron acceptor in the adsorption: Ga2O3, which increases elect
props.statement: CO2 acts as an electron acceptor in the adsorption: Ga2O3, which increases electron availability in ZnO, increases the heat of adsorption, and Li2O, which depresses the Fermi level, decreases it; a high electron concentration in the adsorbent increases the strength of the adsorption bond.

props.name: Plotted against surface coverage (moles/m2), the CO2 heats of adsorption on the
props.statement: Plotted against surface coverage (moles/m2), the CO2 heats of adsorption on the three adsorbents diverge as coverage decreases: very marked differences at low coverage, barely any at high coverage.

props.name: The hydrogen heats of adsorption are in an unexpected order for the three adsorb
props.statement: The hydrogen heats of adsorption are in an unexpected order for the three adsorbents and appear to increase with coverage; whether this is significant or due to erroneous readings caused by reduction cannot be said with any certainty.

props.name: Hydrogen also reduced the zinc oxide at the temperatures used: the zinc deposit
props.statement: Hydrogen also reduced the zinc oxide at the temperatures used: the zinc deposit in the adsorption tube and the darkening of the pellets are strong evidence for reduction and help refute intra-lattice adsorption; the hydrogen isotherms were most unsatisfactory because of reduction effects.

props.name: CO2 isotherms obey the Langmuir equation reasonably well only above about 0.3 mm
props.statement: CO2 isotherms obey the Langmuir equation reasonably well only above about 0.3 mm Hg; the Freundlich equation holds for CO2 on ZnO and on ZnO + Ga2O3 from 10-2 to 1 mm Hg but not on ZnO + Li2O; CO isotherms obey Langmuir fairly well above about 0.3 mm Hg and never obey Freundlich.

props.name: For the adsorbent with the lowest Fermi level, ZnO + 0.5 mole % Li2O, the reduct
props.statement: For the adsorbent with the lowest Fermi level, ZnO + 0.5 mole % Li2O, the reduction effect of CO was most marked, so that equilibrium pressures could not be measured even for the smaller adsorptions.

props.name: Although the adsorbents were prepared by as closely similar methods as possible,
props.statement: Although the adsorbents were prepared by as closely similar methods as possible, addition of 0.5 mole % Ga2O3 almost doubled the surface area of the zinc oxide and 0.5 mole % Li2O increased it; the reason is at present obscure.

props.name: Because of thermomolecular flow the heats of adsorption are a little below their
props.statement: Because of thermomolecular flow the heats of adsorption are a little below their true values; a 4% error is the largest possible (recalculation for H2 on ZnO + Ga2O3 at 1.5 x 10-6 moles/gm showed 14.2 Kcal per mole to be only 4% too low); relative values between the three adsorbents are correct.

props.name: The Fermi level in the adsorbent is of primary importance in determining the hea
props.statement: The Fermi level in the adsorbent is of primary importance in determining the heat of CO2 adsorption only at low coverage; at higher coverage other factors such as repulsive interactions between molecules become more important.

props.name: In the reduction by hydrogen water would be formed and most probably rapidly ads
props.statement: In the reduction by hydrogen water would be formed and most probably rapidly adsorbed.

props.name: The rapid extra adsorption of hydrogen on lowering the temperature (Frankenburg'
props.statement: The rapid extra adsorption of hydrogen on lowering the temperature (Frankenburg's method) is explained by two types of adsorption sites, one with negligible and one with considerable activation energy of adsorption; either the new state is true equilibrium, or equilibrium on the high activation energy sites is frozen in, so that only the highest temperature isotherm represents true equilibrium.

props.name: Reduction of the zinc oxide by carbon monoxide was taking place: above a certain
props.statement: Reduction of the zinc oxide by carbon monoxide was taking place: above a certain CO pressure the reaction rate becomes measurable, the CO2 produced is immediately adsorbed (causing the continued pressure drop), and the zinc formed darkens the adsorbent and sublimes to the cooler parts of the apparatus (the deposit).

props.name: pure ZnO from zinc oxalate
props.method: precipitation of zinc oxalate from zinc chloride and ammonium oxalate, drying and heating in air
steps: Just less than the stoichiometric quantity of zinc chloride was added slowly to a hot concentrated solution of ammonium oxalate
the precipitate of zinc oxalate was filtered off and washed with distilled water
heated in a stream of air in a tube furnace at 450°C for 10 hours
all batches were mixed together to form one homogeneous stock
powders compressed into tablets of diameter 5.5 mm and thickness 1 - 2 mm

props.name: ZnO + 0.5 mole % Ga2O3 by impregnation with gallium nitrate
props.method: paste of ZnO stock with gallium nitrate solution, dried and heated to decompose the nitrate to the oxide
props.note: 'heated as before' refers to the ZnO preparation (450 °C in air); the source does not restate the temperature
steps: Spectroscopically pure gallium was dissolved in concentrated nitric acid
the solution was evaporated almost to dryness several times to remove most of the excess acid
the gallium nitrate was dissolved in distilled water and made into a paste with zinc oxide powder from the stock prepared previously
the paste was dried and heated as before to decompose the gallium nitrate to gallium oxide
powders compressed into tablets of diameter 5.5 mm and thickness 1 - 2 mm

props.name: ZnO + 0.5 mole % Li2O by impregnation with lithium oxalate
props.method: paste of ZnO stock with lithium oxalate solution, dried and heated to decompose the oxalate to the oxide
props.note: lithium oxalate was chosen to keep the preparation conditions the same for all three; no black carbon particles were observed under a microscope
steps: Lithium oxalate was dissolved in distilled water and made into a paste with zinc oxide powder
The paste was dried, and heated as before to decompose the oxalate to the oxide
powders compressed into tablets of diameter 5.5 mm and thickness 1 - 2 mm
